parent: grape based wine or wine-like food product
label: grape wine
definition: An alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes.

label: red wine
definition: A type of wine made from dark-colored grape varieties.
comment: The actual color of the wine can range from intense violet, typical of young wines, through to brick red for mature wines and brown for older red wines.[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_wine]

label: rosé wine
definition: A type of grape wine that incorporates some of the color from the grape skins, but not enough to qualify it as a red wine.

label: white wine
definition: A wine that is fermented with little or no grape skin contact.
comment: A wine whose color can be straw-yellow, yellow-green, or yellow-gold. It is produced by the alcoholic fermentation of the non-coloured pulp of grapes, which may have a skin of any colour.

label: table wine (US)
definition: A grape wine which is neither fortified, nor sparkling, nor expensive.

label: Table Wine (deprecated EU standard)
definition: A European Union wine category replaced by the Protected Geographical Indication in 2011.
comment: The lower of two overall quality categories, the higher of which is Quality Wines Produced in Specified Regions (QWPSR). All levels of national wine classification systems within the EU correspond to either TW or the QWPSR, although the terms that actually appear on wine labels are defined by national wine laws with the EU regulations as a framework.[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Table_wine]

label: fortified wine
definition: A wine to which a distilled spirit, usually brandy, has been added.

label: still wine
definition: Wine produced by a method of vinification that leaves it free from carbon dioxide and therefore not sparkling or effervescent.

label: Quality Wines Produced in Specified Regions
definition: A Protected Geographical Status appellation which identifies a wine with either Protected Geographical Indication or a Protected Designation of Origin.
comment: The European Union regulates and defines the status of quality wines" according to production method, management and geographical location. Its original, fundamental role is in differentiating quality wines from table wines."[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quality_Wines_Produced_in_Specified_Regions]

label: Denominazione di origine controllata
definition: An Italian wine quality assurance label for food products and especially wines (an appellation), and for various formaggi.
comment: It is modelled after the French AOC. It was instituted in 1963 and overhauled in 1992 for compliance with the equivalent EU law on Protected Designation of Origin, which came into effect that year .[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denominazione_di_origine_controllata].

label: Vintners Quality Alliance
definition: A regulatory and appellation system which guarantees the high quality and authenticity of origin for Canadian wines made under that system in British Columbia and Ontario.

label: American Viticultural Area
definition: A designated wine grape-growing region in the United States, providing an official appellation for the mutual benefit of wineries and consumers.

label: Spanish wine production framework
definition: A food product appellaction framework pertaining to Spanish wine.

parent: Quality Wines Produced in Specified Regions|Spanish wine production framework
label: Denominación de Origen Protegida
definition: The mainstay of Spain's wine quality control system. Each region is governed by a consejo regulador, which decides on the boundaries of the region, permitted varietals, maximum yields, limits of alcoholic strength and other quality standards or production limitations pertaining to the zone.
comment: As of 2019 there are 96 DOPs that are subdivided into DOCa, DO, VP, and VC. The sub-categories can be called DOP, or they can use the traditional terms of DOCa, DO, VP, and VC.  In 2016, the use of the term Denominación de Origen (DO) was updated to Denominación de Origen Protegida (DOP).[wikipedia]

label: Denominación de Origen Calificada
definition: The highest category in Spanish wine regulations, reserved for regions with above-average grape prices and particularly stringent quality controls.
comment: Rioja was the first Spanish region to be awarded DOCa status in 1991, followed by Priorat in 2003. Priorat uses the Catalan language DOQ, for denominació d'origen qualificada. These are the only two regions considered above" DO status."[wikipedia]

label: Vino de Pago
definition: A special term for high-quality, single-estate Spanish wines which in some cases also have DOP or VC or IGP appellations.
comment: Pago is a Spanish term for a vineyard estate ...This category was formed in 2003.[wikipedia]

label: Vino de Calidad con indicación geográfica
definition: A category of spanish wine that does not fully meet the stringent standards of the DOP category, but are above the standards of the IGP category.

parent: Protected Geographical Indication|Spanish wine production framework
label: Indicación geográfica protegida
definition: An EU Protected Geographical Indication which includes Spanish wines below the DOP level, and is wine originating from a specific place, a region or a country, which has a certain quality, reputation or other characteristic - including production phases - that can be essentially attributed to its geographical origin, at least one of which takes place in the defined geographical area.
comment: These can use the traditional term Vino de la Tierra (VT).[wikipedia]

label: Vino de Mesa
definition: Any wine from unclassified Spanish vineyards, and wine that has been declassified by blending.
comment: This includes both inexpensive jug wines and some expensive wines that are not yet classified due to innovation outside traditional lines.[wikipedia]

label: Appellation d'origine contrôlée
definition: A food product appellation framework authorized for certain French geographical indications for wines, cheeses, butters, and other agricultural products, all under the auspices of the government bureau Institut National des Appellations d'Origine (INAO). [Wikipedia]

label: Denominación de origen
definition: A food product appellation framework which is a regulatory geographical indication system used primarily for foodstuffs such as cheeses, condiments, honey, and meats, among others.
comment: In wines, it parallels the hierarchical systems of France (1935) and Italy (1963), although Rioja (1925) and Jerez (1933) preceded the full system.[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denominaci%C3%B3n_de_origen]

label: Protected Geographical Status
definition: A food product appellation framework defined in European Union law to protect the names of regional foods.
comment: Protected Designation of Origin (PDO), Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) and Traditional Speciality Guaranteed (TSG) are geographical indications, or more precisely regimes, within the framework. The law (enforced within the EU and being gradually expanded internationally via bilateral agreements of the EU with non-EU countries) ensures that only products genuinely originating in that region are allowed in commerce as such. The legislation came into force in 1992. The purpose of the law is to protect the reputation of the regional foods and eliminate the unfair competition and misleading of consumers by non-genuine products, which may be of inferior quality or of different flavour. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geographical_indications_and_traditional_specialities_in_the_European_Union#Protected_geographical_indication_(PGI)]

label: Protected Designation of Origin
definition: A Protected Geographical Status which covers agricultural products and foodstuffs which are produced, processed and prepared in a given geographical area using recognised know-how.

label: Protected Geographical Indication
definition: A Protected Geographical Status covering agricultural products and foodstuffs closely linked to the geographical area.

label: Traditional Speciality Guaranteed
definition: A Protected Geographical Status which highlights traditional character, either in the composition or means of production.

label: wine by region
definition: A grape wine distinguished by the region its grapes were grown in.

label: Beaujolais wine
definition: A French Appellation d'Origine Contrôlée (AOC) wine generally made of the Gamay grape which has a thin skin and is low in tannins.

label: Bordeaux wine
definition: Any wine produced in the Bordeaux region of southwest France.

label: Zakynthos wine
definition: Zakynthos Wine is wine produced on the Greek island of Zakynthos (Zante) in the Ionian Sea. A wide array of native Ionian grape varieties have been planted on the island for centuries, and are most famously used to make the intensely flavored, highly acidic Verdea wine.

label: Reserve wine
definition: Reserve wine is wine of a higher quality than usual, or a wine that has been aged before being sold, or both. Traditionally, winemakers would reserve some of their best wine rather than sell it immediately, coining the term.

label: Chablis wine
definition: Chablis wine is a wine made in the Chablis region of France.

label: Cabernet Sauvignon wine
definition: A Cabernet Sauvignon wine is any wine produced using only Cabernet Sauvignon grapes. It often appears with Merlot and Cabernet Franc in blended Bordeaux wines.

label: Cabernet Sauvignon grape cultivar
definition: The Cabernet Sauvignon grape cultivar originates from a cross between Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon blanc varieties. It produces Cabernet Sauvignon grapes, a red wine grape variety.

label: Chardonnay wine
definition: Chardonnay wine is wine produced using only Chardonnay grapes.

label: Chardonnay grape cultivar
definition: The Chardonnay grape cultivar is the result of a cross between the Pinot noir and Gouais blanc (Heunisch) grape varieties. It produces a green-skinned grape variety used in the production of white wine.

label: Chenin blanc wine
definition: A Chenin blanc wine is any wine produced using only Chenin blanc grapes.

label: Chenin blanc grape cultivar
definition: Chenin blanc grapes are a White wine grape variety from the Loire Valley of France. Its high acidity means it can be used to make everything from sparkling wines to well-balanced dessert wines, although it can produce very bland, neutral wines if the vine's natural vigor is not controlled.

label: Malbec wine
definition: A Malbec wine is any wine produced using only Malbec grapes.

label: Malbec grape cultivar
definition: Malbec grapes are a purple grape variety used in making red wine. The grapes tend to have an inky dark color and robust tannins, and are known as one of the six grapes allowed in the blend of red Bordeaux wine. The French plantations of Malbec are now found primarily in Cahors in South West France. It is increasingly celebrated as an Argentine varietal wine and is being grown around the world.

label: Merlot wine
definition: A Merlot wine is any wine produced using only Merlot grapes.

label: Merlot grape cultivar
definition: Merlot is a dark blue-colored wine grape variety, that is used as both a blending grape and for varietal wines.

label: Pinot blanc wine
definition: A pinot blanc wine is any wine produced using only Pinco blanc grapes.

label: Pinot blanc grape cultivar
definition: Pinot blanc is a white wine grape. It is a point genetic mutation of Pinot noir.

label: Pinot gris wine
definition: Pinot gris is a white wine varietal produced only from Pinot gris grapes.  The Italian synonym, Pinot Grigio, has become strongly associated with lighter wines produced in great quantities, particularly in northern Italy.

label: Pinot gris grape cultivar
definition: Pinot gris is a white wine grape variety (mutation) of the Pinot family which shares its genetic fingerprint with Pinot Noir, Pinot Blanc et al. . Pinot gris is grown around the globe with the "spicy" full-bodied Alsatian and lighter-bodied, more acidic Italian styles being most widely recognized.

label: Pinot noir wine
definition: Pinot noir wine is a red wine varietal made only from Pinot noir grapes.  The thin skins and low levels of phenolic compounds lends pinot to producing mostly lightly colored, medium-bodied and low-tannin wines that can often go through phases of uneven and unpredictable aging.

label: Pinot noir grape cultivar
definition: Pinot noir grape is a red wine grape variety. The name is derived from the French words for pine and black. The word pine alludes to the grape variety having tightly clustered, pine cone-shaped bunches of fruit. Pinot noir grapes are grown around the world, mostly in the cooler climates, and the grape is chiefly associated with the Burgundy region of France.

label: Pinotage wine
definition: Pinotage wine is a red wine varietal produced only from Pinotage grapes. This type of wine can range from a fairly cheap, light-bodied red wine with some funky aromas (including extremes such as acetone, paint, rubber, and at times banana) all the way to full-bodied red wines with balance, elegance, fully developed black fruit flavors, and an enduring, sweet, smokey finish.

label: Pinotage grape cultivar
definition: Pinotage is a red wine grape that is South Africa's signature variety. It was bred there in 1925 as a crossbetween Pinot noir and Cinsaut. The grape is a viticultural intraspecific cross of two varieties of Vitis vinifera, not an interspecific hybrid.

label: Riesling wine
definition: Riesling wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Riesling grapes, and offered as dry, semi-sweet, sweet, and sparkling white wines. Riesling wines are usually varietally pure and are seldom oaked.

label: Riesling grape cultivar
definition: Riesling grape is an aromatic white grape variety displaying flowery, almost perfumed, aromas as well as high acidity.

label: Sangiovese wine
definition: Sangiovese wine is a red wine varietal produced only from Sangiovese grapes. It is prized for its high acid, firm tannins and balanced nature. Savory flavors of dark cherries and black stonefruit are characteristic, and may be backed by secondary notes of tomato leaf and dried herbs.

label: Sangiovese grape cultivar
definition: Sangiovese is a red Italian wine grape variety that derives its name from the Latin sanguis Jovis, "the blood of Jupiter".

label: Sauvignon blanc wine
definition: Sauvignon blanc wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Sauvignon blanc grapes.  Its primary fruit flavors are lime, green apple, passion fruit and white peach. Depending on how ripe the grapes are when the wine is made, the flavor will range from zesty lime to flowery peach.

label: Sauvignon blanc grape cultivar
definition: Sauvignon blanc is a green-skinned grape variety that originates from the Bordeaux region of France. The grape most likely gets its name from the French words sauvage ("wild") and blanc ("white") due to its early origins as an indigenous grape in South West France.

label: Semillon wine
definition: Semillon wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Semillon grapes.  The primary fruit flavors in Semillon wine are lemon, apple, pear and green papaya. Semillon is France’s 3rd most planted white wine variety behind Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.

label: Semillon grape cultivar
definition: Semillon is a golden-skinned grape used to make dry and sweet white wines, mostly in France and Australia.

label: Glera wine
definition: Glera wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Glera grapes.

label: Glera grape cultivar
definition: Glera is a white variety of grape of Slovenian origin, which was brought to the village of Prosecco from Slovenia's Karst region. Glera was, until 2009, mostly referred to as Prosecco. It is mainly cultivated for use in sparkling Italian wine styles.

label: Prosecco wine
definition: Prosecco is an Italian white wine varietal produced primarily from Glera grapes, but other grape varieties may be included. Prosecco controlled designation of origin can be spumante ("sparkling wine"), frizzante ("semi-sparkling wine"), or tranquillo ("still wine").

label: Syrah wine
definition: Syrah wine is a white wine produced entirely from Syrah grapes.  The wines are often powerfully flavoured and full-bodied.

label: Syrah grape cultivar
definition: Syrah is a dark-skinned grape variety grown throughout the world and used primarily to produce red wine. In 1999, Syrah was found to be the offspring of two obscure grapes from southeastern France, Dureza and Mondeuse Blanche.

label: Tempranillo wine
definition: Tempranillo wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Tempranillo grapes.

label: Tempranillo grape cultivar
definition: Tempranillo is a black grape variety widely grown to make full-bodied red wines in its native Spain.

label: Zinfandel wine
definition: Zinfandel wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Zinfandel grapes.  A classic wine is high in both alcohol and tannins, intensely flavored and deeply colored.

label: Zinfandel grape cultivar
definition: Zinfandel is a variety of black-skinned wine grape.

label: Frappato wine
definition: Frappato wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Frappato grapes.  As a varietal, Frappato produces light bodied wines with a distinct grapey aroma.

label: Frappato grape cultivar
definition: Frappato di Vittoria or Frappato is a red Italian wine grape variety planted primarily in Sicily.

label: Gamay noir wine
definition: Gamay noir wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Gamay grapes.

label: Gamay grape cultivar
definition: Gamay is a purple-colored grape variety used to make red wines, most notably grown in Beaujolais and in the Loire Valley around Tours.

label: Gewürztraminer wine
definition: Gewürztraminerwine is a white wine varietal produced entirely from Gewürztraminer grapes.

label: Gewürztraminer grape cultivar
definition: Gewürztraminer is an aromatic wine grape variety, used in white wines, and performs best in cooler climates.

label: Carignane wine
definition: Carignane wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Carignane grapes.

label: Carignane grape cultivar
definition: Carignan (also known as Carignane) is a red grape variety of Spanish origin that is more commonly found in French wine but is widely planted throughout the western Mediterranean and around the globe.

label: Grenache wine
definition: Grenache wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Grenache grapes.

label: Grenache grape cultivar
definition: Grenache is one of the most widely planted red wine grape varieties in the world.

label: Barbera wine
definition: Barbera wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Barbera grapes.

label: Barbera grape cultivar
definition: Barbera is a red Italian wine grape variety that, as of 2000, was the third most-planted red grape variety in Italy (after Sangiovese and Montepulciano). It produces good yields and is known for deep color, full body, low tannins and high levels of acid.

label: Blaufränkisch grape cultivar
definition: Blaufränkisch (German for blue Frankish) is a dark-skinned variety of grape used for red wine.

label: Blaufränkisch wine
definition: A red wine varietal produced entirely from Blaufränkisch grapes.

label: Mourvèdre grape cultivar
definition: A red wine grape cultivar variety that is grown in many regions around the world including the Rhône and Provence regions of France, the Valencia and Jumilla denominaciones de origen of Spain, as well as the Balearic Islands, California and Washington and the Australian regions of South Australia and New South Wales, as well as South Africa.

label: pressed grape juice
definition: Grape juice which is extracted from grapes using a grape pressing process.
comment: Pressed juice often has lower acidity levels, higher potassium and pH level, more phenolic compounds such as tannins and more suspended solids such as natural gum and proteins. [wikipedia:Pressing_(wine)#Free-run_versus_pressed_juice]

label: free-run grape juice
definition: Grape juice which has been extracted through the process of crushing, the natural break down of the grape cell walls during maceration or fermentation, and/or by the weight of grapes within a tall container.

label: grape pomace
definition: The solid remains of grapes after crushing or pressing, typically containing pulp, skins, stems, and seeds.
comment: Grape pomace contains the skins, pulp, seeds, and stems of the fruit, and has traditionally been used to produce pomace brandy.     [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pomace]

label: grape must
definition: A grape berry food product which is the juice of freshly pressed grapes that contains some amount of pulp, skins, stems, and seeds.
comment: Grape pomace components typically comprises between 7 to 23 percent of the total weight of must. [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Must]

label: destemmed grape must
definition: A grape berry food product which results from crushing whole (destemmed) grapes and which contains grape juice and components of grape pomace.

label: red wine must
SubClassOf: 'is specified output of' some ('extended maceration' and 'has specified input' some 'red grape cluster')
definition: A grape must made from red wine grapes which are substantially macerated.

label: white wine must
definition: A grape must made from red or white wine grapes and which has insignificant masceration.

label: rosé wine must
SubClassOf: 'is specified output of' some ('limited maceration' and 'has specified input' some 'red grape cluster')
definition: A grape must made from red wine grapes which are partially macerated.

label: Muscat wine
definition: A red wine wine varietal produced from the Muscat grape variety, that is known for its aromatic and sweet characteristics.

label: red Burgundy wine
definition: A red wine varietal produced in the Burgundy region of France, primarily made from the Pinot Noir grapes.

label: Muller Thurgau
definition: A white wine varietal that originated in Germany, created by crossing Riesling and Madeleine Royale.

label: Petite Sirah wine
definition: A red wine varietal, characterized by spicy fruitiness and bold tannins, made from the Petite Sirah grape variety.

label: Cabernet Franc wine
definition: A red wine varietal made primarily from the Cabernet Franc grape, characterized by its herbaceous and fruity flavors.

label: late harvest wine
definition: A wine that is made from grapes that are harvested later than usual.

label: tagliatelle
definition: Tagliatelle is a traditional type of egg pasta from the Emilia-Romagna and Marche regions of Italy. Individual pieces of tagliatelle are long, flat ribbons that are similar in shape to fettuccine and are typically about 6.5 to 10 mm (0.26 to 0.39 in) wide.

label: tortellini
definition: Tortellini are ring-shaped pasta, sometimes also described as "navel shaped", hence their alternative name of "belly button" (ombelico). They are typically stuffed with a mix of meat (pork loin, raw prosciutto, Mortadella), and Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.

label: tortelloni
definition: Tortelloni are stuffed pasta, the same shape as tortellini, but larger. They are usually stuffed with ricotta cheese and leaf vegetables, such as spinach.

label: tortiglioni
definition: Tortiglioni are a type of pasta, similar to rigatoni but larger and with deeper grooves which spiral around the pasta.

label: fusilli
definition: Fusilli are a variety of pasta that are formed into corkscrew or helical shapes. The word fusilli presumably comes from fuso ("spindle"), as traditionally it is "spun" by pressing and rolling a small rod over the thin strips of pasta to wind them around it in a corkscrew shape.

label: conchiglie
definition: Conchiglie, commonly known as "shells" or "seashells" is a type of pasta. It is usually sold in the plain durum wheat variety. The shell shape of the pasta allows the sauce to adhere to it.

label: linguine
definition: Linguine is a type of pasta similar to fettuccine and trenette but elliptical in section rather than flat. It is about 4 millimetres in width, which is wider than spaghetti but not as wide as fettuccine.

label: cannelloni
definition: Cannelloni are a cylindrical type of lasagna generally served baked with a filling and covered by a sauce in Italian cuisine.

label: penne
definition: Penne is an extruded type of pasta with cylinder-shaped pieces, their ends cut at a bias. It is lexically related to Latin penna (meaning "feather" or "quill"), and was originally intended to imitate the then-ubiquitous fountain pen's steel nibs.

label: CANNED FOOD
EquivalentTo: 'food (canned)' and 'has defining ingredient' some '[part of plant or animal]'
definition: Canned food is a kind of food product which is prepared according to a canning recipe.

label: pineapple (canned)
EquivalentTo: 'food (canned)' and 'has defining ingredient' some 'piece of pineapple'

label: shrimp (canned)
EquivalentTo: 'food (canned)' and 'has defining ingredient' some 'shrimp (raw)'

label: salmon (canned)
EquivalentTo: 'food (canned)' and 'has defining ingredient' some 'salmon (raw)'

label: mussel (canned)
EquivalentTo: 'food (canned)' and 'has defining ingredient' some 'mussel (shell off, raw)'

label: clam (canned)
EquivalentTo: 'food (canned)' and 'has defining ingredient' some 'clam (shell off, raw)'

label: albacore (canned)
EquivalentTo: 'food (canned)' and 'has defining ingredient' some 'piece of albacore meat (raw)'
